data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's causal mechanism ('Coordination Decay' converts catastrophic correlated failure into stochastic degradation) is only specified for one class of cause: internal update/patch propagation. The problem explicitly asks what evidence distinguishes truly independent failures from failures that appear uncorrelated until a shared cause is found; SRC_004's own countercondition concedes an external environmental trigger (leap second) can defeat the mechanism, but the target provides no causal account or evidentiary criterion for that shared-cause pathway. Thus the mechanism is incomplete relative to the problem: it explains how a logic error fails to achieve 100% penetration, but is silent on how to detect or reason about correlated failures arising from external common causes that strike all nodes regardless of coordination decay.
